authorship: AI-authored questions derived from the 70 source-verified claims. Reference statements are editorial corrections, never supplied to generation.

questions.question: How quickly is the Moon moving away from Earth each year?
questions.reference: The Moon is slowly moving away from Earth, by about an inch a year.

questions.question: How does Saturn’s average density compare with water?
questions.reference: Saturn has a lower average density than water.

questions.question: Which planet in the Solar System has the shortest day?
questions.reference: Jupiter has the shortest day of any planet in our solar system.

questions.question: On Venus, which is longer: one axial rotation or one orbit around the Sun?
questions.reference: Venus takes longer to spin once on its axis than to orbit the Sun.

questions.question: How was Neptune’s position predicted before it was observed?
questions.reference: Neptune was located using mathematical predictions, rather than a routine sky survey.

questions.question: What unusual sunrise can an observer see from some places on Mercury?
questions.reference: From some places on Mercury, the morning Sun appears to rise, set, and rise again.

questions.question: Does the Sun rotate faster at its equator or at its poles?
questions.reference: The Sun rotates faster at its equator than at its poles.

questions.question: Are corals animals or plants?
questions.reference: Corals are animals, even though they attach themselves to the ocean floor.

questions.question: What material forms a stony coral polyp’s hard skeleton?
questions.reference: A coral polyp builds a hard outer skeleton of limestone.

questions.question: What microscopic organisms live inside the tissues of many corals?
questions.reference: Many corals have microscopic algae living inside their tissues.

questions.question: What is the average depth of the ocean in kilometres?
questions.reference: The average depth of the ocean is about 3.7 kilometres.

questions.question: In which ocean is the Challenger Deep?
questions.reference: The Challenger Deep is in the western Pacific Ocean.

questions.question: Below approximately what ocean depth is there rarely significant sunlight?
questions.reference: Very little sunlight reaches deeper than 200 metres into the ocean.

questions.question: What is the depth range of the ocean’s twilight zone?
questions.reference: The ocean’s twilight zone lies roughly 200 to 1,000 metres below the surface.

questions.question: Does pumped-storage hydropower generate more or less electricity than it uses for pumping?
questions.reference: Pumped-storage hydropower normally uses more electricity to pump water uphill than it generates on the way down.

questions.question: In what year did the first US hydroelectric plant to sell electricity open?
questions.reference: The first US hydroelectric power plant to sell electricity opened in 1882.

questions.question: In which year did wind overtake hydropower in annual US renewable electricity generation?
questions.reference: Wind overtook hydropower as the largest source of annual US renewable electricity generation in 2019.

questions.question: What did people use river-powered paddle wheels for thousands of years ago?
questions.reference: People used hydropower to grind grain thousands of years before modern electricity generation.

questions.question: What does a photovoltaic cell convert sunlight directly into?
questions.reference: A solar photovoltaic cell converts sunlight directly into electricity.

questions.question: During the day, does air above land or above water heat faster?
questions.reference: During the day, air above land heats up faster than air above water.

questions.question: What do the two Greek roots of the word geothermal mean?
questions.reference: The word geothermal combines Greek words meaning earth and heat.

questions.question: In which year was the Statue of Liberty’s current torch installed?
questions.reference: The Statue of Liberty’s current torch was installed in 1986.

questions.question: How many windows and rays are in the Statue of Liberty’s crown?
questions.reference: The Statue of Liberty’s crown has 25 windows and seven rays.

questions.question: What is at the Statue of Liberty’s feet?
questions.reference: There are chains and a broken shackle at the Statue of Liberty’s feet.

questions.question: What date is on the Statue of Liberty’s tablet?
questions.reference: The Statue of Liberty’s tablet shows 4 July 1776 in Roman numerals.

questions.question: In which year was the metre redefined using the speed of light?
questions.reference: The metre was redefined in terms of the speed of light in 1983.

questions.question: How many caesium microwave oscillations define one SI second?
questions.reference: An atomic second counts 9,192,631,770 microwave oscillations associated with caesium atoms.

questions.question: Did minutes and seconds originate in astronomy or mechanical clockmaking?
questions.reference: Minutes and seconds first arose in astronomy, rather than in clockmaking.

questions.question: In ancient Egyptian summer, were daytime hours longer or shorter than nighttime hours?
questions.reference: Ancient Egyptian daytime hours were longer in summer than nighttime hours.

questions.question: Does NOAA report atmospheric carbon dioxide as a dry-air or a wet-air mole fraction?
questions.reference: NOAA expresses atmospheric carbon dioxide as a mole fraction in dry air.

questions.question: What pre-industrial carbon dioxide reference value does NOAA use, in parts per million?
questions.reference: NOAA uses 280 parts per million as a representative pre-industrial carbon dioxide level.

questions.question: What mainly drives the seasonal cycle of atmospheric carbon dioxide?
questions.reference: Land ecosystems’ photosynthesis and respiration drive most of the seasonal carbon dioxide cycle.

questions.question: What is the exact defined speed of light in a vacuum, in metres per second?
questions.reference: The defined speed of light in a vacuum is exactly 299,792,458 metres per second.

questions.question: How long does sunlight take to reach Neptune?
questions.reference: Sunlight takes about four hours to reach Neptune.

questions.question: How thick is the Statue of Liberty’s copper sheeting?
questions.reference: The Statue of Liberty’s copper skin is only about as thick as two pennies.

questions.question: Approximately how many Earth days does the Moon take to orbit Earth?
questions.reference: The Moon completes one orbit around Earth in about 27 Earth days.

questions.question: Do all parts of Saturn’s rings orbit at the same speed?
questions.reference: Every part of Saturn’s ring system orbits the planet at different speeds.

questions.question: Approximately how many hours does Jupiter take to rotate once?
questions.reference: Jupiter needs about 9.9 hours to rotate once on its axis.

questions.question: How many Earth days are in a year on Mercury?
questions.reference: A year on Mercury lasts 88 Earth days.

questions.question: On Venus, does the Sun rise in the east or the west?
questions.reference: On Venus, the Sun rises in the west, opposite to Earth.

questions.question: How long does sunlight take to reach Neptune?
questions.reference: Sunlight reaches Neptune about four hours after leaving the Sun.

questions.question: Does the Sun rotate faster at its equator or at its poles?
questions.reference: The Sun takes 25 days at the equator; 36 at the poles.

questions.question: What material forms a stony coral polyp’s hard skeleton?
questions.reference: The hard outer skeleton of a stony coral polyp is made of calcium carbonate.

questions.question: Is a coral colony one large animal or many small animals?
questions.reference: Coral colonies are colonies of hundreds to thousands of polyps.

questions.question: How do algae living inside corals benefit from the relationship?
questions.reference: The algae living inside corals receive protection and resources for photosynthesis from the relationship.

questions.question: What is the average depth of the ocean in kilometres?

questions.question: In which ocean is the Challenger Deep?

questions.question: In which year did HMS Challenger first sound the Mariana Trench?

questions.question: At approximately what depth does the ocean’s twilight zone begin?
questions.reference: The ocean’s twilight zone begins at a depth of about 200 metres.

questions.question: Does sunlight normally reach four kilometres below the ocean surface?
questions.reference: Sunlight does not penetrate the aphotic zone below 1,000 metres in the ocean.

questions.question: Does pumped-storage hydropower generate more or less electricity than it uses for pumping?
questions.reference: Pumped-storage hydropower uses more electricity for pumping than it generates.

questions.question: In what year did the first US hydroelectric plant to sell electricity open?
questions.reference: The first US hydroelectric power plant to sell electricity opened in 1882.

questions.question: In which year did wind overtake hydropower in annual US renewable electricity generation?
questions.reference: Hydropower remained the largest annual US renewable electricity source until wind overtook it in 2019.

questions.question: Does a photovoltaic cell have to boil water before generating electricity?
questions.reference: A photovoltaic cell converts sunlight directly to make electricity.

questions.reference: In the daily wind cycle, air over land heats faster than air over water during the day.

questions.question: Which direction does the Statue of Liberty face?

questions.question: What date is on the Statue of Liberty’s tablet?

questions.question: How many hours of daylight and how many hours of darkness did ancient Egyptians use?
questions.reference: Ancient Egyptians divided daylight into twelve parts and nighttime into twelve parts.

questions.question: Does NOAA’s atmospheric carbon dioxide mole fraction include or exclude water vapour?
questions.reference: NOAA’s carbon dioxide mole fraction excludes water vapour in the total air measurement.

questions.question: What pre-industrial carbon dioxide reference value does NOAA use, in parts per million?
questions.reference: NOAA’s pre-industrial carbon dioxide reference is 280 parts per million.

questions.question: Which days are included in NOAA’s weekly carbon dioxide average?
questions.reference: NOAA defines its weekly carbon dioxide average using Sunday to Saturday.

questions.reference: The defined speed of light in a vacuum is exactly 299,792,458 metres per second.

questions.question: How many Earth years does one season on Neptune last?
questions.reference: A season on Neptune lasts for over forty Earth years.
